## Resolution
On the `workflow_dispatch` path, "Create Tag" computed the tag from the raw input
(`git tag "${VERSION#v}"`), pushing an unprefixed tag (e.g. `1.0.0`) while "Create GitHub Release"
ran `gh release create "$VERSION"` with the validated, v-prefixed version (`v1.0.0`). Because the
input description tells users to enter `1.0.0`, the common path produced two divergent tags, and
`gh release create` would create the `v`-tag at the default branch HEAD rather than the pushed
commit. The intended convention is v-prefixed (`on.push.tags: v*.*.*`). Changed "Create Tag" to use
`needs.validate.outputs.version` and push that exact tag, so the pushed tag matches the release tag.
Verified with actionlint + yamllint.

Migrated from v1 `nitpicker-findings.md` (Pass 1, 2026-06-24).
title: Release workflow_dispatch pushes a tag that mismatches the release tag

## Problem

Harness mismatch. Both scripts take their input from `$CLAUDE_FILE_PATH` (`case "${CLAUDE_FILE_PATH:-}" in`, `file="${CLAUDE_FILE_PATH:-}"`). Claude Code delivers hook input as JSON on stdin (`tool_input.file_path`, always absolute); the variable is not provided. The guard also blocks with `exit 1`, which Claude Code treats as a non-blocking error — only exit 2 (or `permissionDecision: "deny"`) blocks a PreToolUse call.

## Evidence

- Feeding the real input shape: `printf '{"tool_name":"Edit","tool_input":{"file_path":"<repo>/src/parser.c"}}' | .claude/hooks/pre-edit-guard.sh` → exit 0 (allowed).
- With the variable forced: `CLAUDE_FILE_PATH=<repo>/src/parser.c .claude/hooks/pre-edit-guard.sh` → prints BLOCKED, exit 1 (still non-blocking).
- Hooks reference (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks): PreToolUse "Can block? Yes — exit 2 blocks the tool call"; "any exit code other than 2" is a non-blocking error; PreToolUse input fields `tool_name`, `tool_input` arrive via stdin.
- post-edit-lint.sh:13 `npm run generate >/dev/null 2>&1 || true` and :18 `npx editorconfig-checker "$file" 2>/dev/null || true` run with an empty path, and stdout of an exit-0 PostToolUse hook is never shown to Claude.
- CLAUDE.md "Hooks" section states the guard "Blocks edits to generated files".

## Impact

The documented protection of src/parser.c, src/grammar.json, src/node-types.json and package-lock.json does not exist; grammar.js edits are not regenerated and EditorConfig/corpus checks never report.

## Fix

Read stdin and fail closed:
```bash
input=$(cat) || exit 2
file=$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -er '.tool_input.file_path // .tool_input.notebook_path') || { echo "pre-edit-guard: unparseable hook input" >&2; exit 2; }
case "$file" in */src/parser.c|*/src/grammar.json|*/src/node-types.json|*/src/tree_sitter/*|*/package-lock.json) echo "BLOCKED: generated/lock file: $file" >&2; exit 2;; esac
```
In post-edit-lint.sh parse the same way, drop every `|| true`, and on generate/editorconfig/corpus failure write the message to stderr and `exit 2` so PostToolUse feeds it back to Claude. Re-fire both hooks with the JSON input above to prove the block and the feedback.

## Resolution
Both hooks now read tool_input.file_path from stdin JSON (parsed with node, no env var) and fail closed. pre-edit-guard exits 2 with a stderr reason for src/parser.c, src/grammar.json, src/node-types.json, src/tree_sitter/* and package-lock.json. post-edit-lint regenerates on grammar.js edits, runs editorconfig-checker and the corpus header/separator check (fixed to match the repo's 80-character lines), and reports every failure via stderr + exit 2 with no `|| true`. Proof, firing the scripts with Claude Code JSON input: guard exit 2 for parser.c, node-types.json, tree_sitter/parser.h, package-lock.json; exit 0 for grammar.js and scanner.c; exit 2 for malformed input and missing file_path. post-edit-lint exit 2 for a corpus file without separators and for src/tree_sitter/array.h EditorConfig violations; exit 0 for describe_blocks.txt and a clean rule file; exit 2 for malformed input. shellcheck -S style clean. The live PostToolUse run on .claude/rules/editorconfig.md completed without feedback.
title: Both Claude Code hooks read CLAUDE_FILE_PATH, which Claude Code never sets — guard never blocks, lint never runs

## Problem

`shellspec_skip_statement`, `shellspec_pending_statement` and `shellspec_todo_statement` make the reason/description mandatory:

```js
shellspec_todo_statement: ($) => prec.right(2, seq("Todo", field("description", choice($.string, $.raw_string, $.word)))),
shellspec_pending_statement: ($) => prec.right(2, seq("Pending", field("reason", choice(...)))),
shellspec_skip_statement: ($) => prec.right(2, seq("Skip", field("reason", choice(...)))),
```

ShellSpec accepts all three without an argument (references.md Helper table lists `Todo` with no argument; the official example uses `Skip # without reason`).

## Evidence

- test/spec/12.skip_spec.sh:67-68 (official ShellSpec example): `Skip # without reason` / `When call foo` parses as `(shellspec_skip_statement reason: (word "When"))` followed by `(command name: "call" argument: "foo")` and `(MISSING ";" [67, 4])`.
- Probe `It 'a'\n  Pending\nEnd` → `(ERROR [0,0]-[3,0] ...)` covering the whole example.
- Probe `Todo` → `(ERROR [0,0]-[0,4])`.
- ShellSpec 0.28.1 `--syntax-check` accepts all three; running bare `Pending` reports "Temporarily pended", bare `Todo` creates a pending example.
- No corpus test covers the argument-less forms (utility_blocks.txt, pending_skip_statements.txt only use quoted reasons).

## Impact

A valid official ShellSpec file mis-parses: the `When` evaluation after a bare `Skip` becomes a plain bash command, so highlighting, folding and any tree consumer see a corrupted example. Bare `Pending`/`Todo` turn the entire enclosing example into an ERROR node.

## Fix

Make the argument optional in all three rules, e.g. `seq("Skip", optional(field("reason", choice($.string, $.raw_string, $.word))))`, and add corpus tests `Skip` / `Pending` / `Todo` each followed by a `When call` line on the next line asserting the next line stays a `shellspec_when_statement`. Verify `tree-sitter parse --quiet test/spec/12.skip_spec.sh` exits 0; if the optional argument still crosses the newline, restrict the argument to the same line (e.g. require it via `token.immediate(/[ \t]+/)` separator) before merging.

## Resolution
grammar.js: the Todo description and the Pending/Skip reasons are now `optional(field(..., argument($)))`. Proof with pinned tree-sitter-cli 0.27.0: generate exits 0; test/spec/12.skip_spec.sh parses with `parse --quiet` exit 0 (previously MISSING ";" at [67, 4]); probes for bare `Skip`, `Pending` and `Todo` give 0 ERROR/MISSING, and a bare Skip no longer consumes the next line (`(shellspec_skip_statement)` followed by `(shellspec_when_statement ...)`). New corpus tests "Bare Skip inside It block", "Bare Pending inside It block", "Bare Todo" and "Bare Skip from official skip example" pass in the repo suite (129/129), and all fail against HEAD's grammar.
title: Bare Skip/Pending/Todo misparse: Skip swallows the next line, Pending/Todo produce ERROR

body:
## Problem

Every ShellSpec argument/description slot is `choice($.string, $.raw_string, $.word)` (grammar.js:84, 103, 125, 146, 164, 179, 203, 213-216, 223, 237-238, 244, 246, 264, 273, 285, 291, 300, 320, 330, 337, 351, 355, 359, 367, 381-382, 392, 400, 407). Bash literals such as `simple_expansion` (`$x`), `expansion` (`${x}`), `command_substitution` (`$(cmd)`), `number` and `concatenation` (`--opt=$y`, `"$a"b`) are excluded.

## Evidence

Probes (pinned tree-sitter 0.27.0, committed parser):
- `When call f $x` → `(shellspec_when_statement function: (word) (ERROR [1,13]-[1,15]) argument: (word))`
- `The output should eq $x` → ERROR inside `shellspec_matcher`
- `The value $x should eq 1` → ERROR inside `shellspec_subject`
- `Assert test $x` → ERROR
- `When call f "$a"b --opt=$y` → ERROR at `$`
- `Include $SHELLSPEC_PROJECT_ROOT/lib.sh` → `(shellspec_directive_statement (ERROR [0,7]-[0,9]) path: (word))`
- `Describe $name` → ERROR
ShellSpec 0.28.1 `--syntax-check` accepts `When call echo $x --opt=$x`.

## Impact

Unquoted variables are idiomatic in shell (`When call add $1 $2`, `Include $SHELLSPEC_PROJECT_ROOT/...`); every such line in a real spec file produces ERROR nodes, breaking highlighting and structural navigation for common code.

## Fix

Add one shared hidden rule and use it in every slot:
```js
_shellspec_argument: ($) => choice($.word, $.string, $.raw_string, $.number, $.simple_expansion, $.expansion, $.command_substitution, $.concatenation),
```
Replace each `choice($.string, $.raw_string, $.word)` with `$._shellspec_argument`, regenerate, and add corpus tests for `$x`, `${x}`, `$(cmd)` and `--opt=$y` in When/The/Assert/Include/Describe.

## Resolution
Every ShellSpec argument slot now uses the `argument($)` helper in grammar.js: word, string, raw_string, number, simple_expansion, expansion, command_substitution. `Include` paths also accept `concatenation`. Known limit: other slots exclude `concatenation`, because bash's concatenation repeat produced unresolvable conflicts in every tested variant, so `--opt=$y` parses without ERROR but as two adjacent argument nodes. Proof: probes `When call f $x`, `The output should eq $x`, `The value $x should eq 1`, `Assert test $x`, `Include $SHELLSPEC_PROJECT_ROOT/lib.sh` (now a concatenation path), `Describe $name` and `When call f "$a"b --opt=$y` all give 0 ERROR/MISSING. New corpus tests "When call with unquoted expansion arguments", "The with expansion subject and matcher", "Assert with expansion argument" and "Include with variable path" pass (129/129) and fail against HEAD's grammar. Parse time stayed linear: 2,360-line file 9.5–12.5 ms vs 8.8–9.7 ms baseline.
title: Unquoted expansions and concatenations rejected in every ShellSpec argument position

body:
## Problem

Three grammar alternatives model syntax that ShellSpec does not accept:
1. `shellspec_hook_block` (grammar.js:131-150): `BeforeEach|AfterEach|BeforeAll|AfterAll|BeforeCall|AfterCall|BeforeRun|AfterRun [label] <statements> End`, with its own conflict `[$.shellspec_hook_block]` (:38). ShellSpec hooks are statements only.
2. The Data "Block style with regular statements" alternative (:197-207): `Data [:modifier] [label] <statements> End`. ShellSpec Data block bodies must be `#|`/`# ` lines.
3. The spaced modifier `seq("Data", optional(seq(":", field("modifier", choice("raw", "expand")))))` (:189, :202, :222). Only `Data:raw`/`Data:expand` (no space) are block openers, and the tokenizer never produces a separate `:` here.

## Evidence

ShellSpec 0.28.1 `shellspec --syntax-check`:
- `BeforeEach 'setup'` / `  echo hi` / `End` → "Syntax error: Unexpected 'End'" (the statement form `BeforeEach 'setup'` passes and runs; `BeforeEach`/`AfterEach` are listed in lib/libexec/grammar/dsls:13-14).
- `Data` / `  echo item1` / `End` → "Syntax error: Data text should begin with '#|' or '# '".
- `Data :raw` / `#|a` / `End` inside an It → "When cannot be defined outside of Example" (not a block opener); `Data:raw` / `#|a` / `End` → OK.
tree-sitter (pinned 0.27.0) parses every rejected form with zero ERROR nodes. The `modifier:` field appears in 0 of 6 probes (`Data :raw …End`, `Data : raw …End`, `Data:raw …End`, `Data :raw 'x'`, `Data : expand "x"`, `Data :expand …End`). Corpus tests encoding the invalid forms: hook_blocks.txt:1-219 (12 block tests), nested_structures.txt:77-188, utility_blocks.txt:1-49, :172-186, :215-254.

## Impact

Editors present invalid spec files as well-formed; node-types.json advertises a `modifier` field consumers can query but never receive; the extra hook-block alternative adds a GLR conflict that exists only to support invalid syntax.

## Fix

delete: `shellspec_hook_block` (:131-150), its `_statement_not_subshell` entry (:50) and conflict (:38); the statements-style Data alternative (:197-207); the `optional(seq(":", field("modifier", …)))` pieces (:189, :222). Keep `choice("Data", "Data:raw", "Data:expand")` + `#|` lines + `End`. Replace the listed corpus tests with statement-form hooks (`BeforeEach 'setup'`) and `#|` Data blocks, regenerate, and confirm `npx tree-sitter test` and the spec-file parse loop pass.

## Resolution
Removed `shellspec_hook_block` (its `_statement_not_subshell` entry and conflict), the Data statements-block alternative and the spaced `Data :modifier` forms, so the unreachable `modifier` field no longer exists. The generator then reported `[command_name, shellspec_data_block]` and `[command_name, shellspec_hook_statement]` as unnecessary, so both were removed, and `[$.shellspec_utility_block]` was added: ShellSpec-specific conflicts went from 3 to 1. Proof: generate exits 0 with only the two pre-existing supertype warnings; the corpus tests for those forms were converted to statement hooks and `#|` Data blocks, and the suite passes 129/129; README "Grammar Structure" and CLAUDE.md now list 26 rules and the current conflicts.
title: Grammar accepts block forms ShellSpec rejects and declares a `modifier` field no input produces

## Problem

Contract axis 1 (declared but not implemented):
- package.json:5 `"main": "grammar.js"` — grammar.js calls the tree-sitter CLI DSL global `grammar()`, so `require('@ivuorinen/tree-sitter-shellspec')` throws.
- package.json:16-17 `files` lists `binding.gyp` and `bindings` — neither exists.
- tree-sitter.json:30-37 declares `c`, `go`, `node`, `python`, `rust`, `swift` bindings — no binding.gyp, bindings/, Cargo.toml, setup.py/pyproject.toml, go.mod, Package.swift or Makefile/CMakeLists.txt exist.

## Evidence

`node -e "require('./')"` → throws at node_modules/tree-sitter-bash/grammar.js:45 `module.exports = grammar({` (ReferenceError: grammar is not defined). `npm pack --dry-run` → 14 files: LICENSE, README.md, grammar.js, package.json, queries/highlights.scm, scripts/post-generate.sh, src/* — no bindings. Package is not yet on npm (`npm view` → E404); release.yml would publish this shape. Axis 2: no tags; baseline = first commit; grammar.js/queries unchanged since 7353f27 — no surface change to classify.

## Impact

`npm install @ivuorinen/tree-sitter-shellspec` (README.md:29-31) yields a package no Node, Rust, Python, Go or Swift consumer can load as a Language; the manifest promises bindings that are not shipped.

## Fix

Add a PreToolUse `Bash` hook that denies (exit 2) commands matching `(sed -i|cp|mv|tee|>|tree-sitter generate)` whose target is under `src/parser.c|src/grammar.json|src/node-types.json|src/tree_sitter/`, allowing `npm run generate`/`npm run rebuild`; extend the Edit/Write matcher to `Edit|Write|NotebookEdit`. - **Scanner header:** src/scanner.c names the upstream file and version and lists every local patch with its reason: renamed entry points, explicit <stdlib.h>, and the deserialize() zero-length reset.

`grep -c` prints `0` and exits 1 when nothing matches, so `|| echo "0"` appends a second line. `FAILING_TESTS` becomes the two-line string `0\n0` on every green run.

## Evidence

Reproduced: `X=$(printf 'a\n' | grep -c b || echo "0")` → value `[0\n0]`; `[ "$X" -gt 0 ]` → rc=2 ("integer expression expected"). At :280 `[ "${FAILING_TESTS:-0}" -gt 0 ] || [ "$TEST_EXIT" -ne 0 ]` the first test errors and evaluates false; the gate survives only through `$TEST_EXIT`, and the report prints a two-line "Failing" value.

## Impact

The failing-count check never works; if the runner ever exits 0 with ✗ lines, the job passes.

## Fix

Use `|| true` instead of `|| echo "0"` on all three greps (test.yml:242-244).

## Resolution
In test.yml's coverage job, the three `grep -c ... || echo "0"` counters (TOTAL_TESTS, PASSING_TESTS, FAILING_TESTS) now use `|| true`, with a comment. `grep -c` already prints 0 on no match, so the old fallback produced "0\n0" and broke `[ -gt ]` comparisons. Proof: actionlint (with its shellcheck integration) and zizmor --offline pass on test.yml.
title: Coverage job's `grep -c ... || echo "0"` yields "0\n0" and breaks the failing-test comparison

## Problem

untyped-dependency-leak. grammar.js opts into `// @ts-check` but imports its base grammar from a module with no type declarations: `const bashGrammar = require("tree-sitter-bash/grammar");`. The value is implicitly `any` and is passed straight into `grammar(bashGrammar, {...})`, so the DSL's generic rule-name typing for `$` is lost.

## Evidence

TypeScript language service on grammar.js:10:29 reports TS7016: "Could not find a declaration file for module 'tree-sitter-bash/grammar'. '.../node_modules/tree-sitter-bash/grammar.js' implicitly has an 'any' type." The line is unchanged from HEAD (7353f27). No `@types/tree-sitter-bash` package exists in node_modules and no local `.d.ts` declares the module. This was missed by the initial types pass and surfaced while applying the argument fix, which references `$._literal` across ~30 slots.

## Impact

`@ts-check` cannot flag a misspelled or nonexistent bash rule reference (e.g. `$._literl`) in the editor; the error only appears later when `tree-sitter generate` fails. Build-time script only — Low.

## Fix

Add `types/tree-sitter-bash-grammar.d.ts` with `declare module "tree-sitter-bash/grammar" { const grammar: GrammarSchema<string>; export = grammar; }` (GrammarSchema from tree-sitter-cli's DSL types) and reference it from grammar.js with `/// <reference path="types/tree-sitter-bash-grammar.d.ts" />`; confirm the TS7016 diagnostic disappears.

## Resolution
Added types/tree-sitter-bash-grammar.d.ts, which declares `module "tree-sitter-bash/grammar.js"` with a default export typed `GrammarSchema<string>` from tree-sitter-cli's DSL types; the specifier matches grammar.js's ESM import. grammar.js references it with `/// <reference path="types/tree-sitter-bash-grammar.d.ts" />`.

Proof: `tsc --noEmit --allowJs --checkJs --noImplicitAny --module esnext --moduleResolution bundler` (typescript 5) on the current grammar.js → exit 0, 0 errors. The same file with only the reference line removed → exit 2, exactly one error: TS7016 "Could not find a declaration file for module 'tree-sitter-bash/grammar.js'". The base grammar is no longer `any`.
title: untyped-dependency-leak: `tree-sitter-bash/grammar` has no declaration, so the base grammar is `any` under @ts-check

## Problem

blanket-suppression. grammar.js declares `// @ts-check` (:8) and suppresses every error on :46 with `// @ts-ignore`. The underlying error is precise: the DSL types `RuleBuilder` as `(…, previous?: Rule)` (node_modules/tree-sitter-cli/dsl.d.ts:58), so `original` is `Rule | undefined`, which `choice()` rejects.

## Evidence

grammar.js:43-46 `_statement_not_subshell: ($, original) => choice(// @ts-ignore\n original, ...)`. No type checker is installed or run (no typescript in node_modules, no tsc in CI); only editors evaluate @ts-check.

## Impact

Any other type error introduced on that line (e.g. a misspelled rule reference) is hidden from the editor check the file opts into.

## Fix

Replace the suppression with a narrowed cast: `choice(/** @type {RuleOrLiteral} */ (original), ...)`, or `// @ts-expect-error previous is optional in RuleBuilder but always set when extending bash`.

## Resolution
Replaced the blanket `// @ts-ignore` on `original` in `_statement_not_subshell` with a narrowed JSDoc cast: `/** @type {RuleOrLiteral} */ (original)`. A comment explains that `original` is optional in RuleBuilder's type but always set when extending bash.

Proof with typescript 5 (`tsc --noEmit --allowJs --checkJs --strict --module esnext --moduleResolution bundler`):
- current grammar.js → exit 0, 0 errors;
- the same file with the cast removed (bare `original`, no suppression) → exactly one error, TS2345 "Argument of type 'Rule | undefined' is not assignable to parameter of type 'RuleOrLiteral'" at that line.

The cast suppresses only that assignment, not every error on the line. Generated output unchanged; tests 134/134.
title: Blanket `@ts-ignore` on the inherited `original` rule
